grammar_concept.title: Advanced Reporting Verbs
grammar_concept.rule: Use specific reporting verbs (suggest, insist, deny, admit, recommend, warn, refuse, offer) instead of always using 'say' or 'tell' — each one carries its own precise meaning and often its own grammatical pattern (suggest + -ing/that, deny + -ing, warn + object + to/not to).
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: Basic reported speech (backshifting tenses after 'said'/'told') is only the starting point — fluent English relies heavily on precise reporting verbs that communicate HOW something was said (as a suggestion, a denial, a warning...), not just WHAT was said.
grammar_concept.example: She suggested going to the beach. He denied breaking the vase. The doctor warned him not to smoke.
grammar_concept.example_translation: Ela sugeriu ir à praia. Ele negou ter partido o vaso. O médico avisou-o para não fumar.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: Depois de aprenderem o reported speech básico, os alunos tendem a continuar a usar sempre "said that" para tudo, mesmo quando um verbo mais específico como "suggested", "denied" ou "warned" comunicaria o sentido de forma muito mais natural e precisa. Além disso, cada um destes verbos tem o seu próprio padrão gramatical — "suggest" nunca é seguido de objeto + infinitivo com "to" ("suggested him to go" está errado), ao contrário do que a tradução direta de "sugeriu-lhe ir" levaria a pensar.
grammar_concept.correction: Escolha o verbo de relato que melhor corresponde à intenção real da fala original (suggest = sugestão, deny = negação, warn = aviso, insist = insistência) e siga o padrão gramatical específico desse verbo, não o padrão genérico de "say"/"tell": suggest + -ing/that, deny + -ing, warn + objeto + to/not to.
grammar_concept.real_world_example: Summarizing a meeting: "The manager suggested postponing the launch, but the client insisted on keeping the original date."

vocabulary.definition_en: to say firmly that something must happen or is true, refusing to accept another view
example_sentences: She insisted on paying for dinner.

vocabulary.definition_en: to say that something is not true, or that you didn't do something
to tell someone about a possible danger or problem in advance
example_sentences: The doctor warned him not to smoke.

exercises.prompt: Complete: She suggested ___ (go) to the beach.
exercises.explanation: "Suggest" é seguido de verbo-ing (ou "that" + oração), nunca de objeto + infinitivo com "to": "suggested going".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "suggested to go" ou "suggested him to go" é o erro mais comum, por tradução direta de "sugeriu ir"/"sugeriu-lhe ir".

exercises.explanation: "Warn" segue o padrão "warn + objeto + not to + verbo": "warned him not to smoke".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Colocar "not" depois de "to" ("to not smoke") é um erro comum de ordem de palavras.

correct_answer: to say that something is not true, or that you didn't do something
exercises.explanation: "Deny" é o oposto de "admit" — significa recusar que algo é verdade ou que se fez algo.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. What did the client insist on?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "the client insisted on keeping the original date."
exercises.transcript: The manager suggested postponing the launch, but the client insisted on keeping the original date, so we had to find a way to make it work.

exercises.prompt: Read: "When questioned, the employee denied taking the money, but later admitted it under pressure." Did the employee tell the truth immediately?
correct_answer: no, he denied it at first
exercises.explanation: O texto diz que ele primeiro "denied taking the money" e só depois "admitted it" — não disse a verdade de imediato.

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "Ela negou ter perdido as chaves."
correct_answer: She denied having lost the keys.
exercises.explanation: "Deny" é seguido de verbo-ing ("denied losing"), nunca de "that" + infinitivo nem de "to" + verbo.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Traduzir para "She denied to have lost the keys" é o erro mais comum aqui.

steps.content: Reporting verbs like "insisted", "denied" and "warned" usually carry the main stress of the reporting clause, since they replace a whole explanation of tone: "She INSISTED on paying", not a flat, evenly-stressed reading.

steps.prompt: Report a real or invented conversation using at least 2 different reporting verbs (suggest, insist, deny, warn, admit, refuse, offer).
Write 3 sentences reporting things people said, using 3 different reporting verbs instead of 'said'/'told' — pay attention to each verb's grammatical pattern.
